name: Balushahi
instructions: 1. Prepare the dough by mixing maida, baking powder, ghee, and curd into a firm, non-kneaded mass. Let it rest for 30 minutes.
2. Divide the dough into small, thick discs and make a depression in the center using your thumb.
3. Prepare a thick sugar syrup (one-string consistency) with sugar, water, and cardamom powder.
4. Deep fry the discs in ghee or oil on very low heat until they turn golden brown and cook through to the center.
5. Immerse the warm fried Balushahi in the warm sugar syrup for 10-15 minutes, ensuring they absorb the sweetness.
6. Remove from the syrup and let them cool until the outer layer crystallizes.
description: Balushahi is a hallmark of Bihari confectionery, often found in local sweet shops. It is cherished for its flaky, layered texture and dense, syrupy sweetness, making it a staple dessert during festivals, weddings, and traditional family gatherings.
